reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it shows an in-store Ulta shopping vlog, with the speaker selecting cosmetics and holiday items, applying coupons, and reporting the subtotal and savings. The Ibotta, Fetch Rewards, and Rakuten references are separate referral or cash-back promotions, not evidence that the shopping or coupon discussion involves a deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: when I do go in, I like to shop with some coupons,
Decided to grab some infallible lip where I got the chocolate scented.
I will be using a 15 off a 50 store coupon plus my manufacturer coupons there.
Join my Ibotta money saving team and start getting cash back today! You'll get up to a $20 bonus:
Enter my referral code, TJ9TM at the sign-up screen and you'll get 3,000 Fetch Points ($3.00 in points!) when you complete one receipt.

opening.argument: The description ties concrete rewards to viewer actions and destinations. It asks viewers to join an Ibotta team while promising a bonus, directs them to enter a referral code at sign-up for points valued at $3, and offers $10 from Rakuten after signing up and using it once. Whatever the in-store shopping content establishes, these are separate low-barrier reward solicitations: join, sign up, enter the code, complete a receipt, or use the service, and receive a stated benefit. The material therefore does more than discuss ordinary products; it presents multiple reward-linked participation opportunities.

citations.quote: Join my Ibotta money saving team and start getting cash back today! You'll get up to a $20 bonus:
Enter my referral code, TJ9TM at the sign-up screen and you'll get 3,000 Fetch Points ($3.00 in points!) when you complete one receipt.
With Rakuten - Ebates you get cash back for your online purchases, you’ll get $10 for signing up after using for the 1st time:

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the rewards “separate” does not remove them from the material presented to viewers. The description places multiple reward offers alongside the video and supplies destinations and a referral code. The defense establishes shopping activity, but shopping activity does not explain away the distinct requests to join, sign up, enter a code, complete a receipt, or use a service for promised benefits.

citations.quote: Enter my referral code, TJ9TM at the sign-up screen and you'll get 3,000 Fetch Points ($3.00 in points!) when you complete one receipt.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted offers describe ordinary cashback and referral promotions, not an unsupported promise of effortless cash extraction. The Ibotta language says viewers can get cash back, and the Fetch language identifies a specific sign-up condition and receipt completion. The quotes do not show deception, a hidden fee, or failure to deliver; they show disclosed promotional terms attached to consumer services.

citations.quote: Checkout Fetch Rewards, and turn any grocery receipt into savings!
With Rakuten - Ebates you get cash back for your online purchases

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together in the promotional material: external destinations, referral mechanics, and unusually easy stated rewards. Viewers are told they can receive a bonus by joining Ibotta, obtain points after entering a code and completing one receipt, and get $10 after signing up and using Rakuten for the first time. The offers pair monetary or monetary-equivalent returns with simple actions and direct viewers outward. That combination warrants treating the reward claims as the central risk, even though the footage also shows cosmetics and coupons.

citations.quote: Join my Ibotta money saving team and start getting cash back today! You'll get up to a $20 bonus:
Enter my referral code, TJ9TM at the sign-up screen and you'll get 3,000 Fetch Points ($3.00 in points!) when you complete one receipt.
Download here https://bit.ly/2Ay6caM

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes the store footage and coupons but does not address the concentration of reward claims and external sign-up pathways in the description. A viewer can encounter offers promising cash, points, or a bonus and be directed to act through links or a referral code. The existence of genuine retail purchases does not make those additional inducements irrelevant.

citations.quote: you’ll get $10 for signing up after using for the 1st time:

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals are not evidence of a scam by themselves. The cited material identifies cashback services, states the required actions, and does not claim guaranteed profit, investment returns, or risk-free income. “Up to” is expressly qualified, and the Fetch offer specifies completing one receipt. The quotes do not establish that any reward is fabricated or that the links conceal a harmful mechanism.

citations.quote: You'll get up to a $20 bonus:
when you complete one receipt.

opening.argument: The apparent shopping vlog also functions as a promotional funnel. The description establishes a relatable money-saving context, then invites viewers to join an Ibotta team, use Fetch with a personal referral code, and sign up for Rakuten in exchange for stated benefits. The ordinary-commerce setting can make those solicitations appear trustworthy, but the viewer-facing outcome is still participation in several external reward programs. The cosmetics and coupon discussion supplies the promotional atmosphere; the linked offers steer viewers toward registrations, code use, receipt submission, and first-time service use.

citations.quote: In this vlog, we are shopping at Ulta, using a $15/50 store coupon I was emailed and some manufacturer coupons.
Join my Ibotta money saving team and start getting cash back today!
Enter my referral code, TJ9TM at the sign-up screen
With Rakuten - Ebates you get cash back for your online purchases

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the vlog’s retail subject as if it defines every viewer-facing message. It does not account for the explicit calls to join, enter a referral code, and sign up for additional services. The coupon narrative may be genuine, but it also gives the reward solicitations a practical money-saving frame and can steer viewers toward the linked actions.

citations.quote: Checkout Fetch Rewards, and turn any grocery receipt into savings!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The shopping frame is not a disguise for an unshown mechanism. The primary activity is expressly described as shopping at Ulta with store and manufacturer coupons, while the additional services are identified by name and their actions are stated. The quotes show advertising or referral promotion, but they do not show that the ordinary-commerce framing conceals fraud or that the promised rewards are unavailable.
